title: Building a Truthful Portfolio
summary: Learn how a portfolio presents selected evidence-backed work while preserving the difference between presentation, provenance, verification, credentials, and completion.
objectives: Explain the purpose of a learner portfolio.
Distinguish editable presentation fields from institutional source facts.
Select work samples that support a clear and truthful professional story.

vocab.def: A learner-controlled presentation of selected work and supporting information within applicable system rules.
A portfolio item connected to an eligible source or evidence record.
How a portfolio item is titled, summarized, organized, reflected on, or displayed.
Institutional information about provenance, verification, identity, competency references, completion, or other governed facts.

sections.heading: A portfolio helps communicate your work
sections.body: A portfolio can help organize selected projects, reflections, evidence-backed artifacts, and work samples for learning and career conversations.

sections.heading: Presentation and institutional facts are different
sections.body: A learner may be able to improve a title, summary, reflection, order, or other presentation details. Those edits do not change the institutional source, verification, competency, credential, or completion facts.

sections.heading: Select evidence for a purpose
sections.body: A strong portfolio does not need every piece of work you have ever created. Choose examples that help explain relevant skills, growth, responsibilities, and contributions.

sections.heading: Preserve provenance
sections.body: Do not rewrite the history of a project or replace the reviewed source with a later version and pretend it was the original reviewed work.

practice.prompt: Can changing a portfolio artifact summary change whether the underlying evidence was verified?
practice.answer: No. Presentation edits do not change canonical verification or provenance.

practice.prompt: Why might you choose three strong artifacts instead of twenty unrelated ones?
practice.answer: A smaller relevant set can communicate your experience and skills more clearly.

quiz.question: What is the portfolio's primary role?
options: Present selected learner work without rewriting canonical evidence or institutional facts
quiz.answer: Present selected learner work without rewriting canonical evidence or institutional facts

lab.objective: Create a simulated portfolio plan selecting three artifacts and defining a truthful title, summary, reflection, and reason for including each.

reflectionPrompt: What would you want a reviewer or employer to understand about you after viewing three carefully selected pieces of work?
